reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous pattern recognition with external XAI tools to robustly identify shared spurious features. Autonomous analysis allows for initial intuitive identification of common values or trends across misclassified instances, while XAI tools provide quantitative, model-based attribution scores to confirm which features are actually driving misclassification. This approach strengthens confidence in detecting spurious correlations that are neither semantically meaningful nor consistently present in ground truth.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the values of each feature across instances 537, 73, and 291 to identify any shared numerical patterns or outliers
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that have identical or nearly identical values across all three misclassified instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any common feature (e.g., high mean radius or compactness) correlates with a known semantic confusion in cancer classification, such as benign vs malignant in early stages
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that are semantically irrelevant or misleading in this classification context

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides globally interpretable feature importance with consistent attribution across instances, helping identify features with high impact in misclassification. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution that reveals how input changes affect predictions, useful for detecting spurious dependencies. Sensitivity analysis directly measures feature impact by ablation, identifying which features, when removed, significantly alter predictions—especially critical for detecting spurious features. Together, these tools validate whether shared features are truly driving misclassifications beyond their semantic relevance.
